answer: A bonded reputation ledger resists Sybils by making each identity expensive to fake and slow to grow. An agent must lock a stake and complete verified work before earning trust; a new identity starts with zero history, so splitting stake across many clones dilutes each one below the threshold for valuable jobs, like a river spread thin across a canyon floor that cannot carve a channel. Misbehavior triggers slashing and a public plume of evidence that follows the stake, so an attacker must pay fresh capital and rebuild time for every fake identity instead of cloning reputation for free.
